children.label: Models consume vast text corpora to predict the next token, learning the statistical patterns of human language.
This phase enables fluent sentence completion but does not yet teach instruction following or task adherence.
Engineers use curated examples of desired conversations for supervised training, often in large quantities.
The model learns to mimic specific tones, formats, and structures, transitioning from autocomplete to chatbot.
Humans rank model responses, and a reward model learns to predict these preferences.
The language model is then optimized to maximize this reward, becoming helpful, honest, and harmless.
RLHF can introduce issues like sycophancy or over-refusal, which researchers are actively addressing.
User interaction occurs with frozen model weights, sampling tokens one at a time from the distribution.
Decoding parameters control creativity and randomness, while the system prompt guides the model's behavior.
Advanced features like tool use and agents operate on top of inference, without changing the core model.
